metadata.evidence_span: We have considered several counterfactual generating methods in the experiments (Section D.2.6, Table 5 in manuscript). Furthermore, following the suggestions of Reviewer VLao, we have included two more counterfactual generating methods: ROAR and C-CHVAE in the Rebuttal PDF (Table 7). They provide insights into the distribution of counterfactuals around the decision boundary. The CCA performance generalizes to a wide range of counterfactual generating methods as well as different counterfactual distributions w.r.t. the decision boundary. Moreover, we have discussed the effect of counterfactual sparsity on CCA performance in Section D.2.6 of the manuscript. We have also implemented DualCFX and included it in the Rebuttal PDF, comparing CCA with DualCFX under one-sided and two-sided counterfactual scenarios (Table 6).
metadata.rationale: The authors have expanded their experiments to include multiple counterfactual generating methods, including those with data manifold constraints (ROAR, C-CHVAE), and have analyzed the impact of counterfactual sparsity and distribution relative to the decision boundary. They also compared their method with a related approach (DualCFX) under different scenarios. However, the response and revision do not explicitly address robustness considerations as suggested by the reviewer, nor do they fully explore the conditions under which attacks succeed or fail in a comprehensive manner. Thus, while significant progress has been made in addressing the concern about variety of recourse methods, some material aspects remain unresolved.
